method_note: Subjective packet-only forecasts for the fixed two-prompt family averages; no inference or outcome access. Vocabulary projections are treated as noisy evidence about raw scalar sign, with actual signed half-reference doses applied, rather than interpreting canonical as intrinsically trait-positive. Paws/tails, cute punctuation, mascot and kawaii vocabulary modestly increase their relevant traits; male versus female projections affect gender more than feline role, and unrelated projections mostly affect uncertainty about coherence and instruction following. Identity questions offer more self-role opportunities; social replies offer more own-voice style and affection; short constrained tasks and attributed fiction strongly attenuate these features. Opposite doses suppress rare traits without assuming a symmetric new persona. Pair effects are mostly additive with limited uncertain complementarity. Joint is assessed as correlated overlap bounded by feline, female and coherence, separately from relevance. All numerical estimates are prior judgments, not observations.
